A user logs in with a token. The login entry point asks the auth code to create a session, the session is saved under that token, and the new session comes back to the caller. I’ll follow that request from the first call to the stored result.

The story has three chapters: login starts the request, auth gives it an expiry, and storage makes the token useful later.

Review frame: source:branch · scope: `agent-suites/fixtures/sample-app/src` · current version: bound branch head

## Step 1 — Login creates a session

A user submits their login. The story starts at `agent-suites/fixtures/sample-app/src/login.ts:5`, where the entry point calls `createSession`. The request moves to `agent-suites/fixtures/sample-app/src/auth.ts:6`, which gives the session its user ID and one-hour expiry. It then reaches `agent-suites/fixtures/sample-app/src/session-store.ts:5`, where the token points to that session, and the login function returns the same value.

The important code follows the request in that order: `login.ts:5` starts it, `auth.ts:6` creates the value, and `session-store.ts:5` stores it.

Reading: a later request with the token can recover the session created by this login.
